citation.title: Optimal positive end-expiratory pressure reduces right ventricular dysfunction in COVID-19 patients on venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: A retrospective single-center study

provenance.quote: This was a retrospective study of all COVID-19 ECMO patients initiated on VV ECMO from March 2020 through November 2021. All patients were hospitalized at OHSU, an academic medical center in Portland, OR with an intensivist-run VV ECMO program
provenance.location: Methods, Study design and setting, para 1

provenance.quote: Prior to January 2021, our VV ECMO program routinely utilized pressure control ventilation with an inspiratory pressure of 10 cm H2O, PEEP of 10 cm H2O, and a rate of 10 breaths per minute.
provenance.location: Methods, Intervention, para 1

provenance.quote: All patients were hospitalized at OHSU, an academic medical center in Portland, OR with an intensivist-run VV ECMO program
provenance.location: Methods, Study design and setting, para 1

provenance.quote: Starting in January 2021, our program switched to an optimal PEEP strategy wherein PEEP was titrated daily using esophageal manometry to an end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure of 0-3 cm H2O throughout the ECMO run
provenance.location: Methods, Intervention, para 1

provenance.quote: Secondary outcomes included ECMO duration, survival to ECMO decannulation, survival to hospital discharge, incidence of barotrauma, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay (LOS).
provenance.location: Methods, Outcome measures

provenance.quote: Of the 69 included patients, 25 were in the standard PEEP group and 44 in the optimal PEEP group.
provenance.location: Results, para 1

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ards_only: population is COVID-19 VV ECMO with median Murray Score 3.75 and the introduction frames the cohort as 'COVID-19 ARDS patients requiring VV ECMO', though no formal ARDS definition is stated — flagged. obese_population: median BMI 39.5 overall (42.5 optimal, 34.2 standard), all arms at or above 30 kg/m2. timing_subgroup unclear: the intervention is defined by the January 2021 program switch, i.e. relative to enrolment/period, not to a clinical reference event with a measurable interval. ptp_target_subgroups: end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure target 0-3 cm H2O; computation method not stated, so classified as absolute positive end-expiratory Ptp. is_longest_reported_mortality set on 'Overall mortality' because it is the only mortality entry; survival to discharge is a discharge-based outcome recorded separately.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No overlap with any COHORTS.md cluster. Single-center study at OHSU, Portland, OR, USA; enrolment March 2020 to November 2021; no trial registration. The only other VV-ECMO report in the pool, boesing_2024b, is from a different centre (Mannheim) with a different population; no shared authors or institution with any cluster in COHORTS.md.
unclear_items: population.age / baseline_by_arm.age: Table 1 reports a single value per arm with no dispersion and does not state whether mean or median; value_type left null.
eligibility.criteria.adults_18_plus: no explicit age criterion stated; coded yes because the setting is plainly an adult ICU/ECMO program.

population.ards_status: cohort defined as COVID-19 ECMO patients, not formally by an ARDS definition; coded all_ards on the introduction's framing ('COVID-19 ARDS patients requiring VV ECMO') and Murray Score 3.75, but no ARDS definition is applied.
outcomes (Overall mortality): the paper does not state whether 'Overall mortality' is hospital or ICU mortality or a fixed-day mortality; recorded as not_reported timepoint.
intervention.ptp_computation.method: the paper does not state how transpulmonary pressure was computed from esophageal pressure.
intervention.balloon_calibration: no information on balloon filling, calibration, or position verification.
design.consecutive_enrolment: coded true from 'all COVID-19 ECMO patients initiated on VV ECMO', an inference from the 'all patients' framing rather than an explicit consecutive-enrolment statement.
extraction_flags.general_notes: Retrospective cohort with a before/after programmatic change (January 2021) as the basis of the two groups; confounding by calendar period (Delta variant) and by proning and BMI differences is acknowledged by the authors. Esophageal manometry technique (device, calibration, Ptp computation) is entirely unreported. Discharge location distribution (Table 3) recorded here as having no dedicated schema field: 'Discharge location (n, %) — Home (22, 31.9), SNF (14, 20.3), Transfer (2, 2.90) [All Patients]'.
